card.name: Auxiliary verb after a long subject
card.fires_on: The helper verb (have, was, did, also) right after a long noun phrase, just before a past participle such as been reported, taken or observed. It is common in drug-label findings and in 'would/may have' phrasing.

modes.label: Reported findings
modes.description: 'have been reported' or 'was observed' after a list of effects or levels in a label.
modes.example: lowered mexiletine plasma levels<< have>> been reported.

modes.label: Hypothetical would/may have
modes.description: 'have' after would or may, before been or taken in general prose.
modes.example: Fiber optics allow ear surgeons to perform delicate operations that would<< have>> been unheard of just decades ago.

modes.label: Negated or other auxiliary
modes.description: 'did' or 'was' used as the helper verb before a participle or 'not'.

card.writes: It suppresses past-tense action verbs (had, occurred, did, came), which suggests the helper verb is being followed by a participle instead.
card.plain: It fires on the small helper verb in phrases like 'have been reported' or 'would have been', right before the past participle.
